title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: France hit by a nationwide strike over living costs and cuts
stories.summary: Unions called a national strike Thursday; 70,000 police deployed. Marches in Marseille, Lyon, Grenoble and Paris. Rail, hospitals, schools, ports and air traffic join.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: People pressing their own government from below.
stories.what_it_means: French workers and students are pressing their own government over wages, schools and cuts.
stories.economic_impact: Trains and ports disrupted; public debt near 120% of output; belt-tightening budget still stuck.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the whole apartment building knocking on the landlord's door at once over the rent hike.

stories.headline: China talks up a three-leader meeting at APEC
stories.summary: Beijing says it is "in communication" on a China–Russia–US heads-of-state meeting at APEC in Shenzhen (Nov 18–19). Not confirmed.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Power concentrates in a three-leader room.
stories.what_it_means: Three nuclear powers may sit down to divide influence while China also steers Middle East talks.
stories.economic_impact: Brent near about $96 Thursday as diplomacy headlines swing.
stories.everyday_example: It's like three big landlords meeting to redraw who collects rent on the block.

stories.headline: Canada sells sovereignty while courting EU associate status
stories.summary: Budget titled Masters of Our Destiny. Ottawa pushing to become the EU's first associate member; talks aimed at around June 2027.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: A sovereignty slogan over deeper bloc integration.
stories.what_it_means: Ottawa sells independence in the title while tying deeper into Brussels rules it doesn't write.
stories.economic_impact: Deficit still in the roughly $63–70 billion range; a gas-tax cut was extended.
stories.everyday_example: It's like putting "I'm independent" on your jacket while moving back into your parents' house for the free fridge.

stories.headline: White House pushes a Donroe Doctrine in the Americas
stories.summary: White House amplified a Donroe Doctrine line after the midterms: cartels, Venezuela after Maduro, Greenland defense ties, Cuba pressure, keeping China and other outside powers out.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.what_it_means: The old Monroe idea is back on the table: this hemisphere is our lane.
stories.economic_impact: More US-linked trade and security deals may follow; dollar figures still thin.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighborhood watch telling outside gangs the block is closed.

stories.headline: Iran mines unauthorized Hormuz routes; tankers catch fire
stories.summary: IRGC said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire after ships used an unauthorized southern route; one hit a mine. Claims not independently verified. Separately, a tanker was struck by two projectiles off Qatar.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: One government gating a shared energy route.
stories.what_it_means: Iran is treating a shared world energy lane as its private gate.
stories.economic_impact: Brent near about $96 Thursday; shipping and insurance costs stay high.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighbor mining the only road to the grocery store and fining anyone who takes a side path.
